firing.source:
declare const value: unknown;
export const Bad = typeof value == 5;

findings.message: A typeof expression always produces a string, and `5` is not one, so this comparison is always false (always true for != and !==) and the branch behind it is dead or unconditional. Compare against the string instead: `typeof value === "undefined"`, not `typeof value === undefined`.

clean.source:
declare const value: string;
export const Ok = value === 'array';
